output.summary:
Deterministic result, preserved exactly: run_validity = VALID, analysis_coverage = COMPLETE (no reasons), policy_verdict = NO_POLICY, findings = [] (empty). The capacity summary reports bound_type LOWER_BOUND on the load axis "users" with lower_inclusive = 20, upper_exclusive = null, capacity_knee = null (knee_reason KNEE_DETECTOR_NOT_IMPLEMENTED — a fixed product limitation, not a run defect and not an operator action) and capacity policy_verdict = NO_POLICY. All three stages reached their targets exactly (achieved = target = 5 / 10 / 20 users via p05_10s, 30 of 30 complete bins, target_tolerance_ratio 0.1) and each carries verdict PASS with verified_bound_load 5 / 10 / 20. So "at least 20 concurrent users" is a verified floor, not a maximum; no upper bound was established.

Every window_policy_summary shows business_verdict PASS with resource_verdict NO_POLICY. The only business rule referenced is overall error_rate_ratio <= 0.01, observed numerator 0 in all three windows (window denominators 30399 / 36581 / 45668 samples over 300,000 ms spans). The only resource rule referenced is a generator CPU-throttle guard (rule_id generator-cpu-throttle-ratio, operator gt, threshold 0.2, effect diagnostic) that PASSed in all three windows (max observed ratios 0.0594 / 0.1485 / 0.13). A diagnostic guard is diagnostic by contract: it neither creates an upper bound nor converts resource_verdict NO_POLICY. NO_POLICY therefore stays NO_POLICY — only a configured policy or required capacity can yield PASS or FAIL, and a healthy business window, a rerun, or a fixed generator cannot change that.

Measurement scope matters here. Run-scope metrics cover 132,623 samples with 0 errors over a 1,101,102 ms run (p50 94 ms, p95 202 ms, p99 298 ms, max 2406 ms) and six per-transaction summaries use the same full-run denominator. No window-scoped latency or error percentile is referenced, so per-stage latency behaviour at 5, 10 and 20 users is unknown; the run-scope percentiles blend all three stages plus the periods between them. Run-scope counts and window-scoped denominators are different scopes over different spans and must not be compared as inconsistencies.

Timing: clock_alignment is "not_verified_by_core", so no lead/lag or temporal causal ordering may be inferred from these data; clock verification comes first. The evaluation span is 1,040,000 ms (1790634210000 to 1790635250000); the three 300,000 ms stage windows account for 900,000 ms, leaving two 70,000 ms gaps inside the evaluation span. The snapshot span (1790634100000 to 1790635330000) starts 68,783 ms before run start and ends 60,115 ms after run end, with zero dropped leading/trailing cells and millis. Within each window every referenced resource series has expected_cells 30, observed_cells 30, missing_cells 0, longest_gap_cells 0.

Load delivery was exact and flat (jmeter_active_threads min = max = mean = 5 / 10 / 20, standard deviation 0, slope 0). Across windows, checkoutservice mean cpu_cores rose 0.0472 -> 0.0592 -> 0.0675 cores and paymentservice 0.0122 -> 0.0141 -> 0.0150 cores, while frontend mean cpu_cores was nearly unchanged (0.1843 -> 0.1845 -> 0.1871 cores); no resource limits or thresholds for these entities are referenced, so headroom and saturation cannot be judged. Zero errors, flat series, and empty findings do not prove stability, spare capacity, low load, or the absence of a problem. This advice interprets the evidence only and does not alter the deterministic verdict.

hypotheses.observation: policy_verdict is NO_POLICY at analysis level and in the capacity summary, while all three stages (r1-users5, r1-users10, r1-users20) carry verdict PASS with verified_bound_load 5 / 10 / 20, bound_type LOWER_BOUND, lower_inclusive 20 and upper_exclusive null. Each window_policy_summary reports business_verdict PASS together with resource_verdict NO_POLICY.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: No required-capacity or run-level business policy appears to be configured for this run, and the only resource rule referenced is a diagnostic generator guard. Under the product rules a missing policy or missing required capacity yields NO_POLICY, so the healthy business windows and the verified 20-user floor cannot by themselves produce PASS or FAIL.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Inspect the policy configuration attached to this run and list which rules exist (required capacity, business SLO including any latency rule, SUT resource rules). Then configure the missing policy or required capacity and rerun; confirm the resulting verdict becomes PASS or FAIL rather than NO_POLICY.

hypotheses.observation: Three resource_policy_check entries exist, all with rule_id generator-cpu-throttle-ratio, operator gt, threshold 0.2, effect diagnostic and status PASS for windows r1-users5, r1-users10 and r1-users20. Resource summaries are present for frontend, checkoutservice and paymentservice (cpu_cores, memory_bytes) but no resource_policy_check references those entities, and every window_policy_summary shows resource_verdict NO_POLICY.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: The generator throttle guard is diagnostic by contract and is therefore not counted as a binding resource policy; with no resource rules on the system-under-test entities, resource_verdict remains NO_POLICY. This is a configuration gap, not evidence that the SUT resources were healthy or unhealthy.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Inspect the resource rule set and add resource rules with explicit limits for the SUT entities whose series are already collected (frontend, checkoutservice, paymentservice cpu_cores and memory_bytes), then rerun. Leave the generator guard's effect unchanged: a diagnostic guard never creates an upper bound, and changing it to binding/SLA/enforcing is not a supported remedy.

hypotheses.observation: Window-scoped error policy denominators are 30399 (r1-users5), 36581 (r1-users10) and 45668 (r1-users20) samples, each over a 300,000 ms window; dividing by that span gives implied mean rates of roughly 101, 122 and 152 samples per second (arithmetic on referenced values, not a stored field). Over the same stages jmeter_active_threads means are exactly 5, 10 and 20, checkoutservice mean cpu_cores is 0.0472, 0.0592 and 0.0675, paymentservice 0.0122, 0.0141 and 0.0150, while frontend mean cpu_cores is essentially unchanged at 0.1843, 0.1845 and 0.1871.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: Request rate grows sub-linearly while the user count quadruples, which is consistent with pacing, think-time timers or a fixed loop delay in the load plan rather than with a saturation effect; alternatively the mix of transactions executed per stage may differ. The near-flat frontend CPU alongside rising checkoutservice CPU could also mean the frontend series includes a constant background component or is measured over a different scope. The referenced evidence cannot distinguish these.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Inspect the JMeter test plan for timers, pacing and loop delays, and recompute per-window request rates and per-transaction mix from the raw JTL restricted to each window's epoch span (1790634210000-1790634510000, 1790634580000-1790634880000, 1790634950000-1790635250000). Compare those per-window rates against the per-window cpu_cores series before drawing any scaling conclusion.

hypotheses.observation: The overall maximum latency is 2406 ms and the "cart" transaction also reports max 2406 ms (p50 100, p95 201, p99 291). "home" reports p95 293 ms and p99 462 ms (max 1100 ms); "product" reports p99 665 ms (max 1099 ms); "checkout" p99 299 ms (max 1205 ms). By contrast "add product to cart" reports p50 4 ms, p95 94 ms, p99 96 ms (max 1080 ms) and "reset cart" p50 3 ms, p95 92 ms, p99 97 ms (max 1081 ms). All scopes report error_count 0.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: The single largest sample in the run may belong to the "cart" transaction, given the identical max value. The two-order-of-magnitude gap between the p50 of add-to-cart / reset-cart (3-4 ms) and that of cart / checkout / home / product (99-108 ms) may reflect different measurement scopes in the plan (for example a transaction controller aggregating child samplers versus leaf samplers) or genuinely cheaper operations. Neither is established by the referenced summaries.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Inspect the JTL rows with the highest elapsed values (at or near 2406 ms) together with their label, timestamp and success flag, and inspect the plan's sampler/transaction-controller hierarchy to confirm what each label measures. Map those rows to stage windows using their timestamps.
